summary: Hybrid architecture: ASP.NET Core + DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL serving Unity for Android + iOS, hosted on Fly.io (iad). Estimated $1,550-6,400/month (around the $5,000 budget).

architecture_rationale.text: A modular API service for accounts, billing and persistence plus dedicated game/session servers that scale independently for 15,000 concurrent connections. Over-engineering guard: microservices rejected: 8 engineer(s) cannot absorb the operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Mobile - Unity: Chosen because game engine with rendering/physics loop for project.type=gaming; strong performance (5/5) with priorities.performance=5; one codebase ships both Android and iOS (project.platforms); team already works in csharp (team.languages).

alternatives.why_not: Unity scores higher on performance (fit 10.5 vs 11.1).
Not a game engine (project.type=gaming); no dart in team.languages: ramp-up time and hiring risk (fit 2.4 vs 11.1).

tradeoffs: Licence tiers by revenue (Runtime Fee was cancelled in 2024)

backend.justification: Chosen because strong performance (5/5) with priorities.performance=5; team already works in csharp (team.languages); strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong scalability (5/5) with priorities.scalability=3.

alternatives.why_not: ASP.NET Core scores higher on platform coverage and maintainability (fit 9.2 vs 10.7).
No elixir in team.languages: ramp-up time and hiring risk. ASP.NET Core scores higher on maintainability and platform coverage (fit 7.4 vs 10.7).

database.justification: Chosen because relational integrity and transactions for a gaming domain; strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; strong performance (4/5) with priorities.performance=5. Managed as DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL: managed failover/standby available.

alternatives.why_not: DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL scores higher on maintainability and security (fit 6.2 vs 6.6).
DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL scores higher on maintainability and security (fit 5.5 vs 6.6).
DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL scores higher on availability (fit -1.5 vs -1.5).
Excluded by hard constraint: deployment_model=managed_cloud: self-managed VMs/databases are excluded in favour of managed services.

tradeoffs: Single-writer primary: write scale beyond one large node needs partitioning/sharding
Vacuum and connection pooling need attention at scale

hosting.justification: Chosen because strong performance (5/5) with priorities.performance=5; sticky routing keeps every client of a board/room on the same stateful server; runs the ASP.NET Core (.NET 10 LTS) container as-is; strong cost efficiency (4/5) with priorities.cost=3.

alternatives.why_not: Fly.io scores higher on performance and cost (fit 5.6 vs 5.6).
Game netcode needs UDP; HTTP-only platforms cannot host game servers. Fly.io scores higher on performance and cost (fit 3.4 vs 5.6).
Excluded by hard constraint: deployment_model=managed_cloud is not on-premise.

supporting.justification: Chosen because strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=3; strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=3; strong performance (4/5) with priorities.performance=5; strong maintainability (4/5) with priorities.maintainability=3.

alternatives.why_not: Upstash Redis scores higher on cost (fit 3.0 vs 3.3).
Self-hosting another service when a managed option exists. Upstash Redis scores higher on time-to-market (fit 2.8 vs 3.3).

tradeoffs: Per-command pricing grows with chatty workloads

supporting.justification: Chosen because strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=3; reuses the cache already in the stack; strong performance (4/5) with priorities.performance=5; strong cost efficiency (4/5) with priorities.cost=3.

alternatives.why_not: Adds a separate hyperscaler account next to the fly platform. Hangfire.Redis on the Redis/Valkey cache scores higher on cache and time-to-market (fit 2.5 vs 3.3).
Adds a separate hyperscaler account next to the fly platform. Hangfire.Redis on the Redis/Valkey cache scores higher on cache and time-to-market (fit 2.5 vs 3.3).

tradeoffs: Job durability depends on Redis persistence settings

supporting.justification: Chosen because strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=3; strong performance (4/5) with priorities.performance=5; strong maintainability (4/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong scalability (4/5) with priorities.scalability=3.

alternatives.why_not: ASP.NET Core Identity scores higher on cost and authentication fit (fit 2.7 vs 3.0).
Self-hosting another service when a managed option exists. ASP.NET Core Identity scores higher on cost and time-to-market (fit 1.5 vs 3.0).

tradeoffs: You own password storage, rate limiting and MFA flows

supporting.choice: ASP.NET Core SignalR + Redis/Valkey pub/sub backplane
supporting.justification: Chosen because messages stay inside your own backend and region; full control of the hot path for 15,000 live connections; strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=3; strong performance (4/5) with priorities.performance=5.

alternatives.why_not: ASP.NET Core SignalR + Redis/Valkey pub/sub backplane scores higher on realtime support and concurrency handling (fit 4.0 vs 5.5).
ASP.NET Core SignalR + Redis/Valkey pub/sub backplane scores higher on realtime support and concurrency handling (fit 2.7 vs 5.5).

tradeoffs: Multi-instance fan-out needs a pub/sub backplane (Redis/Valkey)
